goals: Mechanistic: quantify the sensitivity of ELM natural sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) to soil texture across the Upper Iowa agricultural landscape
Validation (weak/indirect): sanity-check simulated water-table depth against sparse USGS wells; note tile-drain validation is impossible in-domain
key_processes: vertical soil water partitioning and gravity sub-surface drainage/recharge
texture-dependent hydraulic conductivity and field capacity controlling drainage flux

model_choice.rationale: Soil texture maps directly onto the per-column SSURGO lever; QDRAI is a native ELM output. Single-column ELM isolates texture control on vertical drainage cleanly.

answerable: Sensitivity of NATURAL vertical sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) to soil texture, holding forcing fixed, using per-column SSURGO soils
Relative ranking of drainage flux across texture classes (sand/alluvium vs loess silt/clay)

not_answerable.aspect: Artificial tile-drain flux (the actual dominant drainage pathway in this basin)
not_answerable.why: ELM has no tile-drainage process; QDRAI represents natural gravity drainage only

not_answerable.aspect: Direct validation of sub-surface drainage magnitude
not_answerable.why: tile-drain flow data is missing in-domain; USGS wells measure water table, not drainage

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (single-axis, by soil texture) with light replication
sampling_strategy.n_justification: The question has ONE categorical driver (texture). N is set by the number of dominant SSURGO texture classes (~5) with 2 replicates each to capture within-class forcing-cell variation; a denser grid would add cost without resolving new mechanism.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Place replicate pairs on the dominant loess uplands (silt loam / silty clay loam, the agricultural matrix) and on valley-bottom alluvial soils (sandier, higher drainage). Keep points within a narrow elevation band so texture, not relief, is the varying factor.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 per texture class — captures NLDAS 12 km cell-to-cell forcing variation while keeping soil as the controlled contrast.

sampling_plan.reason: Dominant agricultural soil of the basin; baseline drainage rate for the fine-textured loess matrix.
Finer, lower-conductivity end member; expected minimum natural drainage / maximum retention.
Heaviest texture end member to bound the low-drainage response of the texture axis.
Intermediate texture to resolve the shape (not just endpoints) of the texture–drainage response.
Coarse, high-conductivity end member; expected maximum natural sub-surface drainage.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place validation columns at well sites; compare warm-started/spun-up ZWT
validation_design.metric: bias (expectation-level check only; sparse points preclude robust statistics)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well density; likely 2-4

validation_design.comparison: none possible — flagged as a validation gap

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: one representative multi-year NLDAS forcing window, native SSURGO soil per column, Fan-2013 WTD warm start + short spin-up

requires_capabilities.capability: Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start + multi-year spin-up
requires_capabilities.why: drainage/recharge are slow states; cold-started columns read ~0 recharge and meaningless ZWT
requires_capabilities.blocks: any credible QDRAI or water-table result

requires_capabilities.capability: gridded soil (SSURGO) per-column ingest with texture classification
requires_capabilities.why: texture is the sole driver; columns must be assigned real texture classes
the basin's dominant drainage pathway is engineered tile drains, not native gravity drainage
requires_capabilities.blocks: answering the question about ACTUAL agricultural drainage rather than natural drainage

requires_capabilities.why: no in-domain drainage observations exist to validate QDRAI
requires_capabilities.blocks: direct validation of the drainage flux

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well / water-table observation ingest + HUC boundary + DEM resolver
requires_capabilities.why: to place columns within the HUC in a controlled elevation band and co-locate validation points
requires_capabilities.blocks: placement and the indirect water-table validation

assumptions: Dominant SSURGO texture classes are loess-derived silt loams/silty clay loams on uplands with sandier alluvium in valleys (typical for this HUC); actual classes to be confirmed from SSURGO.
160 m of relief across the HUC is hydrologically minor for this question, so elevation is held roughly constant rather than stratified.
One representative forcing window within 1980-2018 is adequate; texture contrast is the target, not interannual variability.
open_questions: How many USGS wells fall inside the HUC and are they screened in the shallow aquifer (usable for ZWT comparison)?
Is the scientific interest natural sub-surface drainage, or specifically engineered tile-drain flux? The latter is not representable without a tile-drain scheme.
Should we contrast texture effect under a wet vs dry forcing year to test whether texture control is climate-state dependent?
